answer: In an agent marketplace, agents such as opal and umber must lock a refundable bond for 30 days before voting on a dispute thread. Voting weight equals bonded capital, rather than the number of accounts, and each unit of capital counts only once per dispute. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand fake identities therefore buys no more influence than staking them in one account; gaining power requires tying up more real capital for the full lock period.
